scope: Normalized pure states in Sym^N(C^2), equivalently spin j=N/2. Order means at least t, unless a record explicitly says exact maximal order.

conventions.statement: A pure symmetric state is t-anticoherent iff rho_t=I_(t+1)/(t+1) in the symmetric Dicke basis. This is not I_(2^t)/2^t.
Equivalent condition: every spin multipole of ranks 1,...,t vanishes. Thus t-AC implies s-AC for every 0≤s≤t.
Use normalized Dicke states with excitation number r, mapped to |j,m=j−r>. Some supplied papers reverse the sign of the spin-z convention; reflection r↔N−r preserves AC order.
Order zero is vacuous. No normalized pure one-qubit state is 1-AC.

rigorousRestrictions.statement: The t-qubit reduced matrix must have rank t+1, but a pure symmetric state has reduction rank at most min(t+1,N−t+1).
rigorousRestrictions.proof: The two complementary reductions have the same nonzero Schmidt spectrum. The complement is supported on Sym^(N−t), of dimension N−t+1. Hence t+1≤N−t+1.

rigorousRestrictions.statement: No pure symmetric (2t+1)-qubit state can be t-AC for t≥2.
rigorousRestrictions.proof: If rho_t=I_(t+1)/(t+1), its complement rho_(t+1) has t+1 equal nonzero eigenvalues in a symmetric space of dimension t+2. Thus rho_(t+1)=(I_(t+2)−|phi><phi|)/(t+1) for a normalized symmetric (t+1)-qubit vector phi. Trace one qubit, using Tr_1 I_sym^(t+1)=(t+2)/(t+1) I_sym^t. Comparing with rho_t yields rho_t^phi=I_(t+1)/(t+1). But rho_t^phi has rank at most two because phi has a single-qubit complement. This contradicts t+1≥3.

rigorousRestrictions.statement: The spin-tensor Gram matrix gives a quadratic necessary condition on the number of qubits.
rigorousRestrictions.proof: Put q=floor(t/2). For Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal tensors A,B of ranks at most q, A†B has ranks at most 2q≤t. Anticoherence therefore gives <psi|A†B|psi>=Tr(A†B)/(N+1). The (q+1)^2 vectors A|psi> consequently have a positive diagonal Gram matrix, so they are linearly independent in the (N+1)-dimensional spin space.

rigorousRestrictions.kind: catalogue deduction using referenced restriction-rank lemma
rigorousRestrictions.statement: The odd-order necessary bound implies that a pure 5-AC state needs at least 12 qubits.
rigorousRestrictions.proof: The lower-rank tensor images L≤q span (q+1)^2 orthogonal dimensions. Every rank-(q+1) image is orthogonal to that space because cross products have rank at most 2q+1 and zero scalar part. The restriction-rank lemma applied to the line span{|psi>} gives at least q+2 independent rank-(q+1) images. Therefore N+1≥(q+1)^2+(q+2), or N≥(q+1)(q+2).

rigorousRestrictions.statement: Every 2-AC spin-5/2 density operator has purity at most 13/18. Consequently no pure five-qubit 2-AC state exists.
rigorousRestrictions.proof: The source gives a sum of nine positive localizing blocks equal to 13/18−Tr(rho²), valid for arbitrary complex density matrices of every rank. A pure state would have Tr(rho²)=1.

rigorousRestrictions.statement: A Majorana degeneracy m≥N/2 excludes 1-AC, except the balanced-Dicke class D_(N/2,N/2) for even N. Therefore all higher orders are excluded in the same prohibited classes.
rigorousRestrictions.proof: Rotate the repeated Majorana point to a pole. The spin expectation cannot vanish unless the sole occupied Dicke coefficient is the balanced one.

existenceAndThresholdStatements.statement: For every fixed t, pure symmetric t-AC states exist for sufficiently large N.
existenceAndThresholdStatements.proofOutline: Choose t+1 widely separated Dicke indices near scaled Gauss–Legendre nodes. The finite moment system converges to a nonsingular quadrature system with positive weights. For all sufficiently large N, the weights remain positive and support gaps exceed t, eliminating the off-diagonal constraints.
existenceAndThresholdStatements.caution: The proof does not provide the minimal eventual threshold for each t. The explicitly searched N=t(t+1)(t+2)/6 values are not a proven universal formula for all t.

existenceAndThresholdStatements.statement: The thresholds in PRA92 Fig.4 apply to C_m-symmetric constructions with m>t. Their absence is not a general nonexistence theorem.

cautions: PRA96(2017) Fig.6 states explicitly that missing blocks mean lack of numerical convergence; its lowest-found spins are not all proven impossibility thresholds.
Exact anticoherence requires all ranks1,...,t to vanish. Attaining an individual even-sector minimum only cancels even multipoles and can fail already at order1.
In particular, the N10 and N11 S4 minimizers from the threshold supplement are not pure4-AC states. The even-sector threshold N0(4)=10 is not a full4-AC existence threshold.

Purity thresholds and rank-two/rank-four states in the local2026 mixed-AC manuscript concern mixed states. Only a universal purity bound strictly below1 can be used directly as a pure-state exclusion.

The local2605.29436.pdf is an October2026 revised manuscript. The public arXiv v1 is an earlier, shorter version; the new exact certificate statements should be cited to the local version and pinned companion repository.
The approximate scaling t~2sqrt(j) in Quantum2020 and PRR2022 is numerical evidence, not a universal proven bound.
Counting t(t+2) equations against pure-state parameters is a heuristic because the constraints can be dependent; do not turn that count into a general nonexistence proof.

A Majorana constellation with good packing/geometric entanglement or a numerical spherical-design analogy is not by itself an AC certificate. Validate the reduced identity or every multipole through t.
Existence at a single size need not imply existence at the next size: N4t2 exists and N5t2 is impossible. Distinguish first attainment from eventual existence.
